subject: Hosted API pricing — commit tiers, PO path & preferred vendor form
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@contoso.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API pricing — initial commit tier options and next steps

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our demo and your usage profile, I've outlined the high-level hosted API pricing and commit options below so procurement has the exact figures to review:

- Usage (on-demand): $0.0006 / token (no commitment)
- Committed tiers (monthly):
  - 10M tokens/month => 15% discount off list
  - 25M tokens/month => 20% discount off list
  - 50M tokens/month => 25% discount off list
- Annual committed contract: additional 3% reduction vs comparable monthly committed tier (applies when paid/committed annually)

Two important notes:
1) Discounts apply to token consumption up to the committed tier; overage billed at on-demand or at agreed overage rate.
2) We can structure invoicing as monthly invoices against a committed spend (preferred for forecasting) or purely usage-billed invoices.

I've attached our 2026 rate card and a draft SOW that maps the commitment to onboarding milestones. Could you confirm Contoso's vendor onboarding steps (preferred vendor form, W-9, any insurance certificates) and your PO cadence (Net 30/45/60)? If you can send the preferred vendor form, I'll fill and return.

Next step: once we confirm PO/payment terms and the desired commit tier, I'll circulate the SOW for your review and loop in Finance for any billing exceptions.

Best,
Dylan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
+d: (415) 555-0123
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@contoso.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@contoso.com, Mark Johnson <mark.johnson@contoso.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 10:12:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — initial commit tier options and next steps

Dylan,

Thanks for the breakdown — useful. A few procurement items to flag before we can issue a PO:

- Contoso requires a completed Preferred Vendor Form (attached) and supplier registration in our portal. Please complete the attached PDF.
- Standard PO terms are Net 45. Some internal lines require Net 60 for new vendors; that requires approvals from our Treasury team.
- We need a completed W-9 and proof of insurance (GL/Professional Liability).
- Legal will need to review the SOW and proposed billing language to ensure it maps to our contract templates.

On pricing: procurement will not sign a per-token agreement without an annual committed or capped spend for budget certainty. They prefer a committed $ value or a fixed-tier PO. Can Redwood accept a PO for an annual committed spend and invoice monthly against that PO?

Please complete the attached vendor form and return via the supplier portal link (instructions in the attachment). If there are specific clauses you cannot accept on the SOW, flag them and we'll route to Legal early to avoid delays.

Best,
Elena
Senior Procurement Manager, Contoso
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@contoso.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — initial commit tier options and next steps

Elena — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to work through vendor onboarding. Quick responses below:

- Preferred Vendor Form: please find this in the attachments filled in (I have completed the vendor form and will upload to the portal once you confirm the filename).
- W-9 & insurance: I'll attach W-9; insurance certs we can provide (our broker can produce GL / PL certificates).
- PO and billing: Redwood can accept an annual committed spend PO and invoice monthly against that PO. For clarity: the PO would state the committed $ for the year and we'd apply the tiered discounts against consumption until the committed amount is consumed.
- Net terms: standard is Net 45; Net 60 is possible but requires Finance approval for new customers. If Contoso confirms Net 60 is required, we can escalate for an exception tied to an annual committed contract.

If procurement prefers a fixed-tier PO (e.g., "50M tokens equivalent"), we can map that to a monetary value in the SOW. I'll loop in Neha/ Priyom to coordinate approvals and a customer-facing SOW with explicit billing language.

Next steps:
1) Elena — can you confirm whether Contoso will issue an annual committed PO or a monthly rolling PO against usage?
2) I'll upload the completed vendor form and the draft SOW once we align on PO type.

Thanks — cc'ing Neha and Priyom to get SOW/billing language ready.

— Dylan
From: Mark Johnson <mark.johnson@contoso.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@contoso.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 08:45:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — initial commit tier options and next steps

Dylan/Elena,

Quick legal note from our side:
- We need to see a draft SOW that calls out product (Hosted API), billing model (monthly invoicing against PO), and an SLA statement (latency/uptime).
- Please confirm whether Redwood can commit to a cap on price increases year-over-year; Contoso typically requests a clause limiting price increases to the CPI or a fixed percentage.
- If Redwood requires any specific indemnities or data-processing wording, include that in the draft so our counsel can redline.

If you upload the SOW and the completed vendor form I'll route to our Legal and Treasury for faster review.

Mark
Sr. Counsel, Contoso
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Contoso procurement pushback — proposed concession and approvals needed

Neha / Priyom — recap and ask:

Recap: Contoso wants an annual committed PO or fixed-tier PO, prefers Net 60 for new vendors, and requires a completed vendor form + SOW. Legal also wants a cap/commit on price increases.

Proposal (to keep momentum):
- Offer: increase 50M tier introductory discount by 2 percentage points for the first 12 months (i.e., effectively 27% for year 1).
- Billing: accept monthly invoices invoiced against an annual committed PO.
- Net terms: agree to Net 60 only for annual committed contracts > $250k ARR equivalent (Finance approval required).

Ask:
1) Can Finance sign off on Net 60 for Contoso if we mark as a one-year exception (deal_id HAPI-2026-427)?
2) Neha — can you finalize the SOW language to include: product name, billing flow (monthly invoice vs committed PO), introductory discount for year 1, and a soft cap on price increases (CPI + 2% max)?
3) Priyom — please prepare the vendor form upload bundle (W-9, insurance certificate stub) and the final rate card attachment so I can send the full package to Contoso.

I want to keep this simple for the customer; small concession keeps procurement moving and protects margin.

— Dylan
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@contoso.com>, Mark Johnson <mark.johnson@contoso.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — final proposal, vendor form & SOW attached

Hi Elena / Mark,

Following our exchange, please find attached: 1) Completed Contoso Preferred Vendor Form (Contoso_Preferred_Vendor_Form.pdf), 2) Draft SOW (Redwood_DRAFT_SOW_Contoso_v1.pdf), and 3) Redwood rate card (Redwood_RateCard_2026.pdf).

Summary of the proposal for clarity:
- Pricing: per-token on-demand at $0.0006 / token. Committed tiers as previously described (10M/25M/50M).
- Introductory concession: 50M tier will receive 27% discount for the first 12 months if Contoso signs an annual committed PO.
- Billing & PO: Redwood will accept an annual committed PO and issue monthly invoices against that PO.
- Net terms: standard Net 45. We will accept Net 60 for this account as a one-year exception contingent on an annual committed contract >= $250k ARR equivalent.
- Price increases: proposed cap in SOW language — price increases limited to CPI + 2% annually (see SOW section 4.2).

Next steps:
1) Elena — please confirm whether Contoso will issue an annual committed PO (preferred) or a fixed monthly PO.
2) If OK, sign/initial the SOW and upload the vendor form to your supplier portal.
3) Once SOW is countersigned, Redwood will provision billing and issue the first invoice against the PO.

Happy to hop on a 20-min call if you want to walk the SOW line-by-line.

Thanks and talk soon,
Dylan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Contoso_Preferred_Vendor_Form.pdf (filled), Redwood_DRAFT_SOW_Contoso_v1.pdf, Redwood_RateCard_2026.pdf
